issues.legal_issue: A statutory exemption for newly constructed buildings applies prospectively when the law contains no clear indication of retrospective operation.
material_facts: The petitioner argued that the amendment exempting new buildings from the governing Act did not apply to buildings constructed before the amendment.
The Court agreed that the amendment was prospective and applied only to buildings brought into being after it came into force.
issues.conclusion: The amendment applied only to buildings newly constructed after it came into force, although the petitioner was not permitted to raise that point for relief in this proceeding.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the ordinary presumption that legislation operates prospectively unless there is a clear legislative intent to the contrary. It identified the amendment as Act 13 of 1972; it relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.statutory_interpretation_issue: The court is deciding how a law applies over time.
predicates.exemption_for_newly_constructed_building: The law grants an exemption to buildings on the basis that they are newly constructed.
predicates.no_clear_retroactive_intent: The law contains no clear indication that the exemption applies retrospectively.
predicates.exemption_applies_only_to_post_enactment: The exemption applies only to buildings constructed after the law came into force.

issues.definition: When a court interprets a law granting an exemption to newly constructed buildings and finds no clear retrospective intent, the exemption applies only to buildings constructed after the law came into force.

issues.legal_issue: A party may be denied permission to raise a new legal point in a special leave proceeding when the party's use of time obtained through an undertaking to surrender possession amounts to a repudiation of that undertaking.
material_facts: The petitioner had not raised the legal point in the courts below.
The petitioner had undertaken before the High Court to surrender vacant possession and obtained six months for that purpose.
The petitioner used that time to approach the Supreme Court and decline to give possession.
The Court considered the conduct perilously near a breach of the undertaking and held that the petitioner had forfeited the right to seek permission to raise the new point.
issues.conclusion: The Court refused to permit the petitioner to raise the new legal point in the special leave proceeding.
issues.legal_principle: The Court declined to extend its indulgence to a party seeking to raise a new point where the point had not been raised below and the party had used time obtained on an undertaking to the court to avoid carrying it out. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

rule.if: special_leave_proceeding and new_legal_point_not_raised_below and undertaking_to_surrender_given and time_obtained_under_undertaking_used_to_delay_surrender

predicates.special_leave_proceeding: The matter is a special leave proceeding.
predicates.new_legal_point_not_raised_below: The party did not raise the legal point in the courts below.
predicates.undertaking_to_surrender_given: The party undertook to a court to surrender possession.
predicates.time_obtained_under_undertaking_used_to_: The party used time obtained under the undertaking to pursue further proceedings instead of surrendering possession.
predicates.permission_to_raise_new_point_denied: The court refuses to allow the party to raise the new legal point.

issues.definition: In a special leave proceeding, permission to raise a new point is denied when the point was not raised below and the party used time obtained through an undertaking to surrender possession to delay surrender.
